summary.intent: Plan and begin executing GSD roadmap phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end via /gsd-plan-phase then /gsd-execute-phase, and in parallel spin up a git worktree to start independent phase 69 (Rust FUSE/WinFsp) work.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed fully (research, VALIDATION.md, D-07 scope decision, pattern map, REQUIREMENTS registration, 12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, all coverage gates green, all committed); execution began sequentially on the main tree with Wave 1 (68.2-01, the security-critical SDK read-path gate) independently verified complete (296/296 tests) and Wave 2 (68.2-02) dispatched. A clean origin/main-based worktree for phase 69 was also created and handed off for a separate session.

repo: The plan:pre UI capability gate only fires when the hook registry's `when` condition classifies the phase as a net-new UI surface; the lower-level ui-plan-gate check can report block:true even when no UI hook is active for the phase — only active hooks matter, not the raw check output.
Intel API-SURFACE extraction (§7.9) returns 0 symbols for this monorepo — it's HINT-only, so omit it from planner prompts rather than pass an empty/noise section.
The schema-gate planner contribution is orchestrator-evaluated: skip injecting it when the phase touches zero ORM/DB schema files (e.g., pure SDK/codec/web work).
PATTERNS.md (from the pattern-mapper hook) is not auto-committed — must be committed manually after the pattern-mapper agent returns.

worktree.baseRef defaults to 'head' (reason: baseref-head) for this repo's execute-phase, meaning executor worktrees fork from live HEAD (carrying all PLAN.md files), not from origin/main — verify this before dispatching worktree executors on an unmerged branch.
The gap-analysis.plan-post check's rendered output can contain control characters that break naive parsing; call the check directly rather than parsing the wrapped `rendered` field.

This pnpm monorepo requires each git worktree to run its own `pnpm install`, making per-wave worktree create/merge/cleanup expensive — for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is preferable and equally correct when the planner made same-wave plans file-disjoint.

packages/sdk/src/client.ts: enforceResolved (ROT-07 anti-rollback gate) is now wired at read-path sites resolvePublishedNode (~line 781) and dfsFindFolder child loop (~line 913), alongside the pre-existing write-path gate (~line 1156).

workflow: For security-critical foundational plans, independently re-run the acceptance tests rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported PASS before advancing to the next wave.

When a genuine scope ambiguity is surfaced by research (e.g., D-07's literal wording sweeping in off-path files beyond the stated success criteria), stop and use AskUserQuestion to lock the decision into CONTEXT.md before the planner runs, rather than letting the planner guess.

For independent parallel roadmap phases, create a plain `git worktree add` off a fetched/verified origin/main (not EnterWorktree) so the new phase's session doesn't inherit in-progress planning commits from the branch already being driven in the main checkout.
Non-blocking plan-checker warnings (e.g., grep-only coverage on a redundant safety leg) should still be logged as a todo immediately, independent of whether the user chooses to proceed to execution.

friction: `git fetch` failed from the sandboxed session (no network access to GitHub), requiring reliance on a last-known-good local origin/main ref that had to be manually verified as current.
gsd-tools commit helper repeatedly reports `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit verifiably lands in git log, requiring manual `git log` verification each time.
